stories.summary: Real Madrid are tracking Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah ahead of next summer. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah is on the radar of Real Madrid ahead of next summer, while Chelsea, Liverpool, Arsenal, Manchester United and Manchester City have been alerted to the potential availability of Barcelona defender Jules Koundé. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are tracking Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah ahead of next summer, according to Bild. Los Blancos have scouted the 23-year-old England international as they look to add at least two defensive additions to their squad, following his solid displays in Germany since moving from Liverpool for €35 million in 2025, while previous suitors Arsenal are also monitoring developments.

- Chelsea, Liverpool, Arsenal, Manchester United and Manchester City have been alerted to the potential availability of Barcelona defender Jules Koundé, TEAMtalk reports. Chelsea are actively monitoring the France international, with Xabi Alonso keen on reinforcing his options at right back and the Spanish club looking to raise money to fund their new signings.

- Tottenham Hotspur have added Hull City goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis to their shortlist of future goalkeeping targets alongside Brighton's Bart Verbruggen, according to TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old Greece international has impressed so far, with three clean sheets in five Premier League appearances following his £20 million summer move from Olympiakos.

- Bournemouth will not entertain January offers to sign England midfielder Alex Scott despite interest from Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea, reports BBC Sport. The Cherries intend to hold on to the 23-year-old until at least next summer as he enters the final two years of his contract, with transfer valuation of at least £100 million in their minds.

- Real Madrid striker Endrick could face another loan move in January due to a lack of playing time, according to Diario AS. AS Roma maintain an interest in the Brazilian youngster following his previous spell at Lyon, though upcoming opportunities under new Madrid boss José Mourinho could impact his decision.

Other rumors
- Manchester United are keen to agree a new contract with star midfielder Bruno Fernandes, while Atletico Madrid, Juventus, AC Milan and Galatasaray monitor his situation. (Caught Offside)

- United's chances of signing Barcelona left back Alejandro Balde in January have received a boost due to his reduced game time. (Football Insider)

- Tottenham Hotspur are admiring Brighton & Hove Albion goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen as a potential option for the future. (Ekrem Konur)

- Liverpool are interested in a potential January deal to sign Brentford forward Kevin Schade. (TEAMtalk)

- Liverpool are continuing to keep tabs on Lyon midfielder Tyler Morton following his departure from Anfield last summer. (Football Insider)

- Juventus scouts watched Netherlands international duo Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey during their draw with Germany. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Bayer Leverkusen, Newcastle United, Brentford, Ipswich Town and Hull City are monitoring Dinamo Zagreb defender Noa Mikić. (Ekrem Konur)

- Napoli are preparing a January transfer plan targeting FC Basel winger Asane Sow, Monaco midfielder Mamadou Coulibaly, Rennes midfielder Sebastian Szymański, and Fiorentina defender Dodô. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

stories.headline: 2026 MLB wild-card series Day 3: Live updates, lineups, analysis
stories.summary: One spot in the division series remains. Will the Braves or Phillies keep their season alive?
stories.body:
Three wild-card series were settled in two games -- but one will go the distance.

After the Chicago White Sox, New York Yankees and San Diego Padres all finished their series in sweeps, the NL East showdown between the Philadelphia Phillies and Atlanta Braves will be the only game on wild-card Day 3. And after two dramatic finishes in the first two games -- the Phillies' Game 2 win coming in extra innings -- who knows what's in store for Thursday?

We've got you covered with pregame lineups, sights and sounds from the ballparks and postgame takeaways as each series ends.

Key links: Megapreview | Bracket | Schedule

Philadelphia Phillies vs. Atlanta Braves
Series tied 1-1

8 p.m. ET

Game 3 starters: TBD vs. TBD

What Phillies need to do to win: Keep the clutch hitting going. This Phillies' core has been in a lot of playoff games -- Bryce Harper has played in 40 while in Philly -- so there have been plenty of ups and downs, but they have the experience. Following Game 2, the buzz in the locker room and in postgame interviews shed light on how much confidence and belief this team has, buoyed by a long history of being in big games. The Phils have the starting pitching edge in Game 3, and the middle of the lineup all homered in the comeback win; they just need to keep it up.

What Braves need to do to win: Rely on their experienced lineup. It's smelling like a bullpen game for Atlanta, probably with Grant Holmes starting -- so getting a third standout six-plus-inning starting pitching performance in this series might be asking for too much. The lineup has enough talent to carry this team, and Aaron Nola is notably more hittable than Cristopher Sanchez and Jesus Luzardo, two of the best starting pitchers in the league this season. A little more home-cooked, late-game magic like in Game 1 is easy to imagine.

stories.headline: WNBA playoffs 2026: Caitlin Clark, A'ja Wilson and keys to Fever-Aces Game 3
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts Indiana on Thursday with the winner advancing to the WNBA semifinals. Here's what could decide the game.
stories.body:
LAS VEGAS -- The No. 3 seed Las Vegas Aces are the WNBA's defending champions and out to prove they are still the league's boss. The No. 6 seed Indiana Fever know they're about to be as popular in Vegas as the house constantly winning.

After the Fever's 99-89 win over the Aces on Tuesday in Indianapolis evened their first-round series 1-1, the teams meet Thursday (9 p.m. ET) to decide who moves on to the semifinals. The Aces have won three of the past four championships. The Fever's lone title came in 2012.

Emotions will run high at Michelob Ultra Arena for Game 3. On Tuesday, Aces star A'ja Wilson objected to a fan pointing at her from behind the basket and left the court to confront him.

The WNBA rulebook bars players or coaches from going into the stands to confront spectators, but as of Wednesday night, the league hadn't made a statement about Wilson nor teammate Kierstan Bell, who left the bench during the incident.

Aces fans will be fired up to support their team. The Fever haven't had much luck in Las Vegas until this season. The Aces moved to the city in 2018, and Indiana did not win a game there until July 5, an 84-68 victory. Then the Fever won again, this time 109-75, in Las Vegas a week later.

Indiana almost made it a regular-season sweep on Aug. 6 in Indianapolis but blew a 20-point lead and then fell 86-84 in overtime. Back in Las Vegas for the teams' playoff opener Sunday, the Aces dominated 102-85.

Now the teams meet for the sixth and final time in 2026. Here's what might decide which team moves on. And be sure to come back when the game tips for live analysis, updates and highlights.

Can the Fever replicate Tuesday's defense?

During the regular season, the Fever ranked ninth in defensive rating (estimate of points allowed per 100 possessions) at 110.3, and the Aces were fifth (107.2). Las Vegas was better on both ends of the court in Game 1, and Indiana knew it had to improve its defense Tuesday to keep its season going.

The Fever did that, at times frustrating all the Aces except Jackie Young, whom they could not stop (31 points). The Aces still scored 89 points. But during both the second and third quarters, the Fever held the Aces to 17 points.

That put Indiana in the driver's seat for the fourth quarter. The Aces made a run, outscoring the Fever 29-27 in the final period, but the middle-game defense gave Indiana enough cushion.

"I thought we played with a back-against-the-wall desperation that you need to play with at playoff time," Indiana coach Stephanie White said.

Now they need to do that again.

How well will Wilson play?

It's rare to see Wilson lose her cool, but on Tuesday the Fever defense seemed to frustrate her at times. She was 5-of-11 from the field but 12-of-13 from the line. Wilson was the WNBA's leading scorer in the regular season and is one of the most clutch players in league history. That latter trait could make all the difference in Game 3.

Coach Becky Hammon thought defense was the Aces' biggest problem in Game 2. She said that kept them from being the offensive team they normally are, and that impacted Wilson's performance.

"I thought [the Fever] brought a lot of congestion [in the lane]," Hammon said. "Them picking up, being disruptive, got us out of our flow a little bit. At times, your offense has to help your defense. I thought defensively we were poor tonight, and the two are married together. We know when we're a good defensive team, we become very elite offensively."

Can the Fever guards do enough for a victory?

The backcourt of Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell has been one of the most entertaining shows in the WNBA all season, and it was outstanding Tuesday. Clark finished with 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds. Mitchell had 26 points.

The Fever also got strong defense from two other guards: starter Lexie Hull and reserve rookie Raven Johnson. Their energy was a big part of what helped the Fever rally and then take the lead after trailing 26-18 after the first quarter.

If the guards do their job, the Fever are formidable. But post player Aliyah Boston ultimately could be the difference-maker. She came back after a tough first quarter Tuesday and had 22 points. That was her highest scoring output since also getting 22 on Aug. 22.

Can Indiana slow down Jackie Young?

Young has 52 points and 15 assists through two games of this series. Like her teammates Wilson and Chelsea Gray, Young is a seasoned big-game player. That trio has won three WNBA championships together. And while Wilson is the perennial MVP candidate and Gray is the "Point Gawd," Young also has been indispensable for Las Vegas since being drafted No. 1 in 2019.

Wilson, Young and Gray are Hall of Fame-level players. But the Aces got nine points and five rebounds from starter Stephanie Talbot, too, and that's significant. Jewell Loyd and Cheyenne Parker-Tyus also can provide an offensive boost off the bench to back up the Aces' big three.

stories.headline: NBA preview 2026-27: Five coaches facing the most pressure to win
stories.summary: Which coaches could face the most scrutiny this season? Ben Golliver examines what lies ahead for five with Finals aspirations.
stories.body:
This summer's NBA coaching carousel was largely driven by losing teams seeking a new voice: None of the six teams that made a coaching change won a 2026 playoff series, while four finished more than 10 games out of the play-in tournament races.

Expect a much different dynamic during the 2026-27 campaign. After a busy offseason that saw a laundry list of All-Star players change scenery, the pressure will be ramped up on coaches of teams expected to contend for a title.

With that in mind, let's rank the five coaches facing the most intense scrutiny during the upcoming season, starting at No. 5 with a reigning Eastern Conference finalist.

5. Kenny Atkinson, Cleveland Cavaliers

Atkinson has had more success than almost all his coaching colleagues since he was hired by the Cavaliers in 2024. The former Golden State Warriors assistant followed up a sparkling 64-win season for Cleveland in 2024-25 with a 2026 East finals appearance, the franchise's first without LeBron James since 1992.

Unfortunately, Atkinson's Cavaliers have specialized in crash landings. During the 2025 playoffs, the top-seeded Cavs were blown off the court in the second round by the upstart Indiana Pacers, and Cleveland was largely uncompetitive against the Knicks while being swept out of the 2026 East finals.

How many consecutive agonizing endings can one coach survive? That's the dilemma for Atkinson, who gets the benefit of coaching an expensive and talent-rich roster that boasts strong continuity.

Cavs owner Dan Gilbert showed his continued commitment to winning this summer with generous deals for Donovan Mitchell, James Harden and newcomer Peyton Watson. Meanwhile, Cleveland retained its big man pairing of Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, who will combine to earn $78 million this season despite lineup fit questions and inconsistent playoff performances.

The pieces remain in place for Cleveland to remain among the East's leading contenders. What can Atkinson do to make sure his team puts its best foot forward when it matters most?

4. David Adelman, Denver Nuggets

Warning to all coaches: Beware of the post-championship backslide.

Since winning the 2023 title, Nikola Jokic's Nuggets have traveled a similar path to that of the Milwaukee Bucks after Giannis Antetokounmpo led them to the 2021 title. The Nuggets fired former coach Michael Malone in 2025 once their standard started to slip, just as the Bucks fired former coach Mike Budenholzer in 2023 after a pair of first-round exits.

Now, the attention turns to Adelman, who replaced Malone just days before the 2025 postseason. While Denver nearly reached the West finals in 2025, it lost more ground last season with a perfunctory first-round loss to the undermanned Minnesota Timberwolves.

The Milwaukee comparison casts an ominous shadow: Adrian Griffin, Budenholzer's replacement, was a first-time head coach who didn't last long before he was replaced by a more decorated alternative in Doc Rivers. Like Griffin, Adelman is a relatively inexperienced head coach tasked with contending for titles and shaping the remaining prime years of an MVP-level franchise player. And, like Griffin, Adelman's ability to achieve those goals is complicated by his team's flawed and incomplete roster.

While Denver breathed a major sign of relief Monday when Jokic announced his intention to re-sign with the Nuggets next summer, that doesn't necessarily reduce the pressure on Adelman to reverse the franchise's momentum.

Adelman can't really ask more from Jokic, who averaged a 27-point triple-double last season and finished in the top two in MVP voting for the sixth straight season. The coach can hope for better health for forward Aaron Gordon and a bounce-back season from guard Christian Braun, and Adelman should hope that Denver lands on the opposite side of the playoff bracket from Minnesota.

Still, this is a tall coaching order. The Nuggets have lost Michael Porter Jr. and Watson over the past two offseasons, and this summer's additions -- DeMar DeRozan and Marvin Bagley III -- don't project as game changers. If Denver's playoff progress stagnates despite Jokic's continued brilliance, Adelman could find himself stuck absorbing the heat.

3. Mitch Johnson, San Antonio Spurs

In hindsight, Johnson got off way too easy for how poorly the Spurs performed at times in their NBA Finals loss to the New York Knicks.

Yes, San Antonio's youth and inexperience were serious issues, and franchise center Victor Wembanyama wasn't quite prepared to seize control of the series. But the 39-year-old Johnson's own youth and inexperience were factors too. He refused to change his starting lineup or make major rotation changes as his team continually blew leads, and he completely lost control of the game flow during San Antonio's unforgettable Game 4 loss.

The Spurs are the opposite of a rash organization: Johnson, who succeeded the legendary Gregg Popovich, is their second coach in nearly 30 years. With that said, the youth excuse no longer applies now that Wembanyama is arguably the NBA's best player and after the Spurs won 62 games and eliminated the 2025 champion Oklahoma City Thunder in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals on the road.

Johnson has arguably the NBA's most enviable collection of talent, and San Antonio will return all its key players while adding veteran forward Tobias Harris. The Spurs must sort through how to handle their glut of guards -- De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper -- and refine Wembanyama's offensive impact in late-game situations. While Johnson was entirely unwilling to bench Fox for poor play last season, that's the type of decision that sometimes must be made to maximize a team's potential.

The good news for Johnson is that Wembanyama's presence virtually guarantees an elite team defense and a high playoff seed. What's more, his players appear refocused after their sour Finals finish, and they enjoyed some quality bonding time together in France this summer.

But to whom much is given, much is expected. Johnson must find a way to write a better ending this time.

2. Ime Udoka, Houston Rockets

Jamahl Mosley had the most success of the six coaches who were let go this summer, leading the Orlando Magic to 46 wins and a seven-game first-round playoff series loss to the Detroit Pistons. Ultimately, the Magic concluded that Mosley had been given enough chances and it was Sean Sweeney's turn to try to deliver the franchise's first playoff series win since 2010.

Udoka's path with the Rockets mirrors Mosley's time with the Magic: Udoka has transformed a lottery team into a playoff team, but he has been unable to get out of the first round in multiple tries despite a talented young roster. With Houston committing big dollars to Kevin Durant, Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson, it's officially time for Udoka to translate his team's potential into actualized success.

The good news for Udoka is that veteran guard Fred VanVleet will return to the court after missing last season with a knee injury and Houston didn't lose any crucial rotation players this summer.

The bad news? Serious questions linger about the Rockets' ability to create enough spacing on offense and execute in close games. Udoka, who made his name as a defensive-minded coach, must prove he can find creative answers to the scoring issues.

Houston's collapse in last season's first round against the Luka Doncic-less Lakers was the type of painful defeat that can pull a group closer together or fracture its chemistry. While Udoka has some peace of mind thanks to a lucrative long-term contract extension he signed in 2025, the time has come for the Rockets to turn the corner.

1. Nick Nurse, Philadelphia 76ers

Any coach worth his salt would embrace the challenge and opportunity facing Nurse. Talent is a prerequisite for winning, and the new-look 76ers have assembled an awful lot of it.

Just two seasons ago, Nurse was stuck coaching a hopeless 24-win team that got off to a 2-12 start and could barely keep franchise center Joel Embiid on the court. Nurse survived that trainwreck. He then guided the Sixers to an unexpected first-round playoff series win over the rival Boston Celtics last season, watched longtime general manager Daryl Morey get fired in June and had James and Jaylen Brown fall in his lap. What a truly incredible change of fortune.

Of course, the catch: The 76ers, who haven't reached the Eastern Conference finals since 2001, are now in championship-or-bust mode, and James' presence ensures their team dynamics will face maximum scrutiny.

That could play out in a few different ways. Miami Heat coach Erik Spoelstra withstood an early storm after James' 2010 arrival to guide Miami to two championships. Former Cleveland Cavaliers coach David Blatt didn't make it through his second season with the team once James returned in 2014. With the Los Angeles Lakers, Luke Walton lasted only one season after James' 2018 arrival; the Lakers wound up cycling through four head coaches in the four-time MVP's eight campaigns in L.A.

Nurse, a creative coaching lifer who has paid his dues, has a major accomplishment on his résumé that separates him from Spoelstra, Blatt and Walton: He guided a title team (the 2019 Toronto Raptors) before James joined his team. Though Nurse's circuitous career path has never previously intersected with James, the coach enters their new relationship with preexisting championship validation.

The primary puzzle Nurse must solve on the court is how to distribute touches and shots. James, Brown, Embiid and Tyrese Maxey are all high-usage players, and VJ Edgecombe and Anfernee Simons also are talented scorers. From there, Nurse will need to coax consistent defensive effort from veteran stars accustomed to being surrounded by high-energy role players.

There's also the matter of managing James and Embiid with an eye toward the playoffs. Over the past six seasons, the chronically injured Embiid has averaged 47 games played and James, now 41, has averaged 60 games played. Nurse should prepare four different rotations to handle the two stars' game-to-game availability (both play, neither plays, only James, only Embiid).

Finally, Nurse will operate knowing that Morey, the executive who hired him in 2023, has been replaced by president of HBSE sports Bob Myers and president of basketball operations Mike Gansey. New front office regimes don't always hire their own coaches, but it can be tempting to oust the incumbent if an aspiring contender falls short.

stories.headline: NHL tonight: What to watch as 10 more teams make their season debuts
stories.summary: Here's what you need to know for the matchups this evening, plus stat leaders and more.
stories.body:
Each NHL team's season-opening game is staggered across the first handful of days of the campaign, and Thursday includes the first regular-season action for 10 clubs.

Whether it's an exciting young rookie, a familiar face in a new place, or an iconic new goaltender mask, there's something for all fans in these contests.

Thursday night is also an occasion where it pays to have multiple devices and an ESPN+ subscription, with eight games on the slate. Here's what to watch in each of them:

Buffalo Sabres at Columbus Blue Jackets

7 ET (ESPN+) | CBJ -115, O/U: 6.5

The Sabres ended the NHL's longest postseason drought last season -- and won a round when they got there, for good measure. The Blue Jackets have not played any playoff hockey in six seasons, but have come close recently. Can they their fortunes around? And for those who like to watch elite defensemen, you're in luck: reigning Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski and Norris finalist Rasmus Dahlin will be playing heavy minutes in this one.

Philadelphia Flyers at New Jersey Devils

7 ET (Disney+/ESPN+/Hulu) | NJ -142, O/U: 5.5

Following Tuesday's Battle of Pennsylvania showdown against the Penguins (a 7-0 loss), the Flyers take on their I-95 rivals in North Jersey. Despite the NHL's divisional playoff format, the two teams have met just twice in the postseason since 2005; the Flyers won 4-1 in the 2010 conference quarterfinals and the Devils won 4-1 in the 2012 conference semifinals. In each of those years, the team that won the matchup lost in the Stanley Cup Final.

Tampa Bay Lightning at New York Rangers

7 ET (ESPN+) | TB -142, O/U: 5.5

After a 3-0 loss to the Bruins in their season opener, the Rangers will look to get on track in their home opener at Madison Square Garden. The Lightning's last trip to MSG (Nov. 29, 2025) resulted in a 4-1 win, although they no longer have the services of Darren Raddysh, who had three helpers in that game but was traded to Toronto this summer.

Minnesota Wild at Nashville Predators

8 ET (ESPN+) | MIN -142, O/U: 6.5

Back in the 2026 Olympics, Sweden and Finland squared off in the latest best-on-best duel between international hockey powers. Finland took that round 4-1, backstopped by Juuse Saros, who is the likely starter for the Preds in their season opener. While Sweden's goalie from that game -- Filip Gustavsson -- won't be available for this contest due to injury, his Minnesota creasemate Jesper Wallstedt was also on that Swedish roster, so perhaps he'll be out for some extra revenge in this tilt.

Seattle Kraken at Calgary Flames

9 ET (ESPN+) | CGY -115, O/U: 5.5

Expectations are on the lower side for both of these teams as the season begins, but given the state of the Pacific Division there could be room for one of them to surprise. Of particular note on the Flames side are Matvei Gridin -- who has all the makings of a future superstar -- and Simon Nemec, who arrived this summer with designs on a much larger role than he had in the Devils' defensive logjam.

Chicago Blackhawks at Utah Mammoth

9:30 ET (Disney+/ESPN+/Hulu) | UTA -192, O/U: 5.5

The Mammoth have two rising American stars on their roster in Clayton Keller and Logan Cooley. The Blackhawks have one of the best American players ever in Patrick Kane -- who scored a goal in Tuesday's season opener for Chicago, and made his NHL debut on Oct. 4, 2007. Keller was nine at that time, while Cooley was three.

Beyond that "make everyone feel old" fact, this game will be a good barometer for the Blackhawks as they climb back into the ranks of legitimate contention, as the Mammoth gave the Stanley Cup Finalist Golden Knights a tough series this past postseason.

Florida Panthers at San Jose Sharks

10 ET (ESPN+) | FLA -135, O/U: 6.5

The Panthers are the second oldest NHL roster this season -- the 30.48 average years of age on their opening night roster is just shy of the Los Angeles Kings' 31.13, according to Elite Prospects -- while the Sharks have the fourth youngest, at 26.29. And San Jose can also boast the NHL's youngest captain, 20-year-old Macklin Celebrini, whose meteoric rise in 2025-26 included a star-making turn at the Olympics and setting the franchise single-season scoring record.

Edmonton Oilers at Vancouver Canucks

10 ET (ESPN+) | EDM -198, O/U: 6.5

It's far too early to declare a "shock of the season," but Vancouver's win over Edmonton on Tuesday is certainly an early contender, given expectations for both teams. It was also an entertaining tilt for those who remember the high-scoring Smythe Division shootouts of decades past. Will either team tighten things up, or are fans in for another offensive onslaught?

Reminder: Fans can catch all of the action in the NHL streaming hub and on the ESPN App.

First-round draft picks are the coin of the realm for big NHL trades, and that's been the case for quite some time.

In fact, on Oct. 1 1981, the Colorado Rockies traded their first-round pick in the 1983 entry draft to the New York Islanders in exchange for defenseman Bob Lorimer and forward Dave Cameron.

The Rockies would relocate -- becoming the New Jersey Devils -- prior to the 1982-83 season, and the pick wound up being No. 3 overall.

The player selected by the Isles? Verdun Juniors center Pat LaFontaine, who would go on to have a Hall of Fame career.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton hits out at Ferrari hierarchy in Fred Vasseur defence: 'Point fingers somewhere else'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has reiterated his full support for Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur and said critics should "point fingers somewhere else," suggesting those higher up in the team's hierarchy must also take responsibility for its struggles.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has reiterated his full support for Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur and said critics should "point fingers somewhere else," suggesting those higher up in the team's hierarchy must also take responsibility for its struggles.

Vasseur's job has come under increasing scrutiny over the past month, with reports last week linking ex-Red Bull boss Christian Horner to replace him.

The speculation grew so much Ferrari felt the need this week to clarify that Ferrari's corporate leadership has "full confidence" in Vasseur, albeit via a press conference with the team's head of communications and not through a statement from either company CEO Benedetto Vigna or chairman John Elkann.

"Ultimately, it's not a one-man operation," Hamilton said in a passionate defence of his team boss to TV in Malaysia on Thursday. "If you want to point fingers, point them somewhere else. There are lot of people above that also are a part of it.

"So if you want to take something from this message: Fred's in his position, he's not going anywhere and I'm here to stay with him. And I still believe fully in where we're going."

Speaking to the written media afterwards, Hamilton reiterated: "I think Fred has the full backing.

"There often seems to be a lot of focus on one individual in one role here. And you can see that, obviously, they've switched out lots of different people in Fred's role. But Fred is a fantastic leader.

"He really is the guy to take his team in the right direction. However, there is a structure that's been there for some time. Whether or not that needs looking at moving forward, there are obviously also people above Fred, and it's not about one person.

"Fred has led the team to ... He's helped make changes in this past year, he's helped us get to the second in the constructors' championship. That's a huge step from last year."

Hamilton was then asked if one of the issues Ferrari has is that Vasseur has no financial stake in the race team, unlike his former boss Toto Wolff, who oversees all facets of the Mercedes F1 team.

In reply to whether Ferrari could benefit with a similar structure to Mercedes, Hamilton said: "There are changes that I would make, but I'm not going to talk about what those are. Toto's in a different position to Fred. The structure's a lot different. That's all I can say."

Ferrari has always been subjected to intense scrutiny, attention which has likely only increased the longer the team's title drought has gone on -- the team's last constructors' title was 2008, with its last drivers' title in 2007.

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: Where were today's drivers when F1 last raced at Sepang?

- Max Verstappen steps in for GT race at Portimão amid two F1 triple-headers

Hamilton said the recent reporting about the state of the internals of the team have been wide of the market.

"For me, it's frustrating to see all the negativity. Because you see other people making mistakes, and they don't normally say too much about them," he said.

"We either make the same mistake, or are not perfect and and it's ten times worse for some reason for Ferrari, but that's also to be expected. Given that it's the best brand here, it's the most iconic by far. For me, I don't read a lot, so that has zero effect on me. But of course, when I come into the room and see, it definitely affects individuals on the team.

"Because every weekend they try and show up and do the best job they can, and they don't get it right all the time. Families are messaging you for all the negative things that they're reading when the people back at the factory are reading all those things, even though they're giving their all. It's almost like sometimes you feel like there's nothing you can do right, even when you're giving your all.

"For me, the message is to not read any of the stuff that's being written. Because the fact is, nobody that's writing any of the stuff has actually any clue what they're talking about, because they're not in the team.

"They don't know what's happening behind closed doors. They don't know how hard everybody's working. It's all down to assumptions and opinions."

Vasseur and Hamilton worked together back in Formula 2 before being reunited at Ferrari.

"Fred's been fantastic working with me and I think our relationship as a whole -- even with our bosses -- is in a better place than it ever was," he added to television.

"Fred's made a lot of changes I've asked for already. I think it's not an easy time for Fred so I think it's good that the team came out with that earlier this week. I've also let him know I support him 100%.

"I wouldn't be here without Fred. Swapping him out ... it won't change how the team moves forwards. It would be detrimental to it."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Thursday, Oct. 1

Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: St. Louis up to 2nd place with unbeaten run now at 17 games
stories.summary: Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.

St. Louis (13-6-8) extended its unbeaten streak to 17 matches in MLS play and moved up to second place in MLS' Western Conference table.

New York (9-12-6) entered having conceded just two goals in its last four games, with Ethan Horvath recording three shutouts.

The Red Bulls had won their last two games, but were without rising stars Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall for the game, with the pair away on national team duty for the United States.

Rafael Navarro opened the scoring just five minutes into the game when he redirected Conrad Wallem's header across the goal.

Becher capitalized on a New York turnover deep in its own half to make it 2-0 in the 87th minute. Ostrak sent in a rebound in stoppage time.

Roman Bürki made four saves to earn his third clean sheet of the season for St. Louis.

It was the first time New York and St. Louis have met during the regular season.

St. Louis hosts the LA Galaxy next on Oct. 11, while the Red Bulls play San Diego FC at home the day before.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.
