stories.headline: Ivan: Nathan Cleary can get even better after Dally M
stories.summary: Ivan Cleary has spoken of the horror of watching his son Nathan's leg injury, and a belief he can still get better again after winning his first Dally M.
stories.body:
Ivan Cleary has admitted watching his son Nathan suffer a badly broken leg marked one of the hardest days of his career, feeling the line between father and coach blurred for the first time.

But the veteran Penrith mentor is insistent his son Nathan still has more levels to attain once he returns from his injury, following his landmark Dally M victory on Wednesday night.

Cleary's Dally M triumph completed the Penrith halfback's rugby league box set, having now claimed every major team and individual honour available to him by age 28.

Unable to attend in person after being released from hospital following emergency surgery on his leg, the Panthers halfback collected the game's top honour while in a wheelchair at home.

Coach Ivan also appeared emotional during Nathan's pre-recorded speech, after the trophy was hand-delivered to the halfback earlier in the day.

"His voice perked up from what it's been the past couple of days," Ivan told AAP.

"It's a pretty amazing award. You don't play the game for individual awards, but it's certainly nice to be recognised.

"Particularly this award, it's pretty much the No.1 award in the game."

Reminded that his son had now scaled virtually every possible mountain in the sport, the Penrith coach insisted there were still improvements left in his son's game.

"It's crazy," Ivan said.

"I know he'd say it and I probably think a bit the same. You don't reflect too much when it's still going on. But when you put it like that, it's amazing.

"But I know there is so much more to come as well, and I know he thinks that way as well."

Nathan has received positive early news from surgeons after the operation on his compound fracture and dislocated ankle, as a result of a hip-drop tackle in Sunday's preliminary-final loss to Newcastle.

He will soon undergo surgery on other foot after fighting through a broken bone to play the Knights, but Penrith are hopeful he will be right for round one in 2027.

"Sunday was definitely one of the harder days I have been through," coach Cleary said.

"It's the first time where the line of dad and coach got a bit blurred. And the loss, I guess we have had a lot of good days so you can't have it all your way.

"Very emotional, but life goes on."

Footage has also emerged of fullback Dylan Edwards not only being horrified by the graphic injury at first, but then also trying to stop Nathan from seeing it.

"I was just trying to keep him calm as I could," Edwards said.

"To his credit he is a tough person. And the way he was handling that was incredible.

"It was gut-wrenching, something you're not used to seeing on the footy field."

Edwards, meanwhile, is still hopeful of being able to represent Australia at the World Cup after avoiding knee surgery following a PCL injury in the loss.

"I'm not sure, I have to talk to Kevvie (coach Kevin Walters)," Edwards said, while wearing a brace at the Dally Ms.

stories.headline: Fantasy playbook: NFL Week 4 Shadow Reports, lineup locks and projected scores
stories.summary: An all-encompassing look at the matchups to exploit or avoid and lineup locks in fantasy, as well as projected scores for all NFL games.
stories.body:
Welcome to The Playbook for Week 4, which kicks off Thursday night with a game between the Steelers and Browns.

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule as it stood before the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense.

DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday.

(Editor's note: Projections and rankings will align almost perfectly, but sometimes when a projection is close, a player might be ranked slightly higher or lower because of other factors, including upside or risk. This column is subject to updates during the weekend, although at the very minimum, rankings will be updated on the site and projections will always be updated inside the game leading up to kickoff.)

PIT-CLE | IND-WAS | NE-BUF | NYJ-CHI | JAX-CIN | ARI-NYG | LAR-PHI | GB-TB

TEN-BAL | DAL-HOU | MIA-MIN | KC-LV | DEN-SF | LAC-SEA | DET-CAR | ATL-NO

Pittsburgh Steelers @ Cleveland Browns
Projected score: Steelers 19, Browns 17

Lineup locks: Jaylen Warren

Fantasy scoop: Harold Fannin Jr. busted out with a 7-51-2 receiving line on nine targets in Week 3. The second-year tight end came out slowly with just 21 yards on three targets in Week 1 but improved to a 5-54-0 line on six targets in Week 2 prior to Sunday's big game. Fannin's snaps (85%) and route participation (85%) are up big from last season and his target share (22.0%) is up slightly.

As long as Deshaun Watson continues to play at a passable level, Fannin will be positioned for TE1 fantasy production. He's a fringe top-10 option against a Steelers defense that allowed Mike Gesicki to find the end zone last week.

Over/under: 35.9 (Lowest)

Win probability: Steelers 60% (8th highest)

Indianapolis Colts @ Washington Commanders
Projected score: Colts 26, Commanders 24

Lineup locks: Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, Terry McLaurin, Tyler Warren

Fantasy scoop: Keenan Allen put together a 6-63-1 receiving line on nine targets in Week 3. This, after the veteran receiver totaled a 7-37-0 line on 11 targets during Weeks 1-2. Allen certainly enjoyed a boost in usage with Alec Pierce sidelined, but we've seen this story before. In 2025 with the Chargers, Allen averaged a healthy 7.0 targets per game (22.1% share). However, that allowed him only 10.7 fantasy PPG, most of which came in the first half of the season. In fact, prior to Sunday, Allen had gone 12 straight games with under 11 fantasy points.

Allen won't be an ideal WR3 option in most weeks, but he's on the radar against a Washington defense that has allowed the most catches, touchdowns and fantasy points to wide receivers this season.

Over/under: 49.8 (3rd highest)

Win probability: Colts 58% (10th highest)

New England Patriots @ Buffalo Bills
Projected score: Bills 28, Patriots 21

Lineup locks: Josh Allen, James Cook III, DJ Moore, Dalton Kincaid

Fantasy scoop: Drake Maye was unable to get back on track in Jacksonville last week and now has just one touchdown pass (and six interceptions) on the season. The 2025 MVP finalist has been held under 210 passing yards in all three games, and his efficiency ranks among the worst at the position.

On the plus side, Maye has been dealing with a tough schedule (Seahawks, Steelers, Jaguars), and the slate lightens up moving forward. That includes this week against a Buffalo defense that sits in the top eight in yards, TDs and fantasy points allowed to QBs. Additionally, Maye is on pace for 465 rushing yards, which is up slightly from 2025.

Maye's poor play means he belongs glued to benches this week, but he shouldn't be sent to waivers just yet.

Over/under: 49.3 (4th highest)

Win probability: Bills 74% (5th highest)

New York Jets @ Chicago Bears
Projected score: Bears 23, Jets 21

Lineup locks: D'Andre Swift, Garrett Wilson, Luther Burden III

Fantasy scoop: Breece Hall is expected to miss this game, which positions Braelon Allen as New York's lead back. Allen has served as a clear backup throughout his career and hasn't fared particularly well (3.7 YPC, 4.8 YPT), but he has been busy off the bench this season, totaling 19 carries and five targets through three games. The 2024 fourth-round pick is one of the league's bigger backs and figures to handle primary early down and goal-line work.

Isaiah Davis will also be involved. While he doesn't have any touches this season, he did rack up 64 touches behind Hall last season and has been effective in a small sample of work over his career (5.6 YPC, 6.2 YPT).

Allen should see enough work to warrant flex consideration against a Bears defense that has struggled against backs this season, including Saquon Barkley on "Monday Night Football."

Over/under: 44.3 (11th highest)

Win probability: Bears 58% (11th highest)

Jacksonville Jaguars @ Cincinnati Bengals
Projected score: Jaguars 26, Bengals 24

Lineup locks: Chase Brown, Ja'Marr Chase, Parker Washington, Tee Higgins

Fantasy scoop: Bhayshul Tuten just misses the "lineup lock" cut. The second-year back's rushing production has been about as consistent as you'll see (13-66-0, 13-65-1, 15-73-1), but he's benefited quite a bit from game script -- Jacksonville has been ahead or tied on a league-high 97% of offensive snaps.

Tuten continues to rotate with three other backs. As a result, he has played on only 49% of snaps, has handled just 52% of the runs and been limited to only five targets (a 7% share). Tuten's rushing volume and efficiency are enough to keep him in the RB2 mix, but a boost in receiving work will be necessary to get him to the next level.

Over/under: 49.2 (5th highest)

Win probability: Jaguars 57% (12th highest)

Arizona Cardinals @ New York Giants
Projected score: Giants 24, Cardinals 22

Lineup locks: Cam Skattebo, Jeremiyah Love, Malik Nabers, Michael Wilson, Trey McBride, Isaiah Likely

Fantasy scoop: Love was a bit slow out of the gate to begin his career, but the third overall pick in April's draft is back in the "lineup lock" mix after a big boost in usage and production in Week 3. After playing on 43% of snaps and totaling 95 yards and one touchdown on 25 touches during Weeks 1-2, Love jumped to 63% of snaps and totaled 109 yards (plus one TD) on 26 touches this past Sunday.

It appears that Arizona is ready to lean on Love as its feature back, and he's in a good spot this week against a Giants defense that is allowing 5.1 yards per RB carry this season (third highest).

Over/under: 46.7 (8th highest)

Win probability: Giants 56% (13th highest)

Los Angeles Rams @ Philadelphia Eagles
Projected score: Rams 25, Eagles 22

Lineup locks: Saquon Barkley, Kyren Williams, Puka Nacua, DeVonta Smith, Davante Adams

Fantasy scoop: Jalen Hurts is trending in the wrong direction, having followed up a 25-point fantasy effort in Week 1 with a pair of finishes of QB15 or worse against Tennessee and Chicago over the past two weeks. Hurts did throw five TD passes during Weeks 1-2, but he's thrown three INTs over his last two games -- and his lone score against Chicago last week was a desperation "tush push" to end the first half.

Perhaps most concerning here is a lack of a rebound for Hurts in the rushing department. After leading all QBs in carries and rushing scores during each of the 2021-24 seasons, Hurts took a big step back in 2025. Hurts' dip in rushing led to an eighth-place finish in fantasy PPG last season and he's showing signs that he may repeat as no more than a back-end QB1 this year. (He currently sits at only 16-87-1 through three weeks in 2026.)

Especially against a solid Rams defense, Hurts is a fringe starting option this week.

Over/under: 46.5 (9th highest)

Win probability: Rams 59% (9th highest)

Green Bay Packers @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers
Projected score: Buccaneers 21, Packers 20

Lineup locks: Bucky Irving, Christian Watson, Matthew Golden

Fantasy scoop: With Baker Mayfield sidelined for roughly three weeks, the Buccaneers will turn to Jalon Daniels. The undrafted rookie handled 45 starts across six seasons at Kansas and, while he plays an aggressive game (a class-high 9.3 aDOT last season) and adds value with his legs (a career 345-1977-23 rushing line), he has a long way to go as a passer (only a 62% completion rate and a class-high 15.3% off-target rate during his career).

Daniels' dual-threat ability makes him a fantasy deep sleeper, but Tampa Bay's passing volume and efficiency are likely to take a sizable hit. Top receiver Emeka Egbuka is on the flex radar against the Packers, but there's a ton of risk here and no other pass catcher should be in lineups.

Over/under: 41.3 (14th highest)

Win probability: Buccaneers 55% (14th highest)

Tennessee Titans @ Baltimore Ravens
Projected score: Ravens 30, Titans 16

Lineup locks: Lamar Jackson, Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers

Fantasy scoop: Mark Andrews makes for a very tricky evaluation. On the one hand, his usage has been excellent, as he's had a target share in the 24-25% range in all three games. In fact, his 24.7% target share for the season is his highest since he was fantasy's No. 4 scoring tight end in 2022. On the other hand, the heavy usage hasn't converted to much fantasy production, as he's turned his 18 targets into only a 13-122-0 receiving line. Andrews has now gone 10 consecutive games below 11.0 fantasy points.

Game scripts will be better at times (Baltimore has been ahead on 65% of its offensive snaps and Jackson is thus just 26th in pass attempts), but this is still a team that will be ahead a lot and will run the ball often. (They're the game-script-adjusted second run-heaviest offense through three weeks).

Andrews is best valued as a fringe TE1 and isn't overly appealing this week against a Titans defense that has allowed a total of only 48 yards on 18 TE targets this season.

Over/under: 45.5 (10th highest)

Win probability: Ravens 91% (2nd highest)

Dallas Cowboys @ Houston Texans
Projected score: Texans 25, Cowboys 25

Lineup locks: Javonte Williams, CeeDee Lamb, Nico Collins, George Pickens

Fantasy scoop: After producing 79 yards and three touchdowns on 23 touches in Week 1, David Montgomery has totaled a mere 70 yards (and zero TDs) on 21 touches during Houston's last two games. Montgomery (37 carries and seven targets on 111 snaps) has struggled badly with efficiency (2.8 YPC), plays a limited role as a receiver (seven targets) and continues to split the Houston backfield with Woody Marks (22 carries and eight targets on 90 snaps).

Montgomery did hit a season-high snap share in Week 3 (65%), but Marks remained plenty involved and handled the team's lone goal line carry. Montgomery is, at best, a fringe RB2 against Dallas.

Over/under: 50.0 (2nd highest)

Win probability: Texans 51% (Lowest)

Miami Dolphins @ Minnesota Vikings
Projected Score: Vikings 26, Dolphins 12

Lineup locks: Kyler Murray, Aaron Jones Sr., Justin Jefferson

Fantasy scoop: De'Von Achane (ACL) is done for the 2026 season, which opens the door for Ollie Gordon II and Jaylen Wright to battle it out for work in the Miami backfield. Wright was sidelined in Week 3, which allowed Gordon to play on 82% of offensive snaps. He wasn't particularly effective (17-41-1 rushing, 3-3-14-0 receiving) and is now averaging an ugly 2.7 yards per carry and 3.8 yards per target on 100 career touches.

Wright, who handled 70-plus touches in both of the past two seasons, had a long look as a lead back in Week 14 last season and delivered 24-107-1 on the ground, but was held without a catch on three targets.

The healthier of the two backs, Gordon is the preferred option of these two for the moment, but neither is a particularly appealing flex in Miami's low-scoring offense and against a Minnesota defense that is allowing 3.1 yards per carry and the third-fewest RB fantasy points.

Over/under: 38.3 (15th highest)

Win probability: Vikings 93% (Highest)

Kansas City Chiefs @ Las Vegas Raiders
Projected score: Chiefs 27, Raiders 22

Lineup locks: Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III, Ashton Jeanty, Rashee Rice, Brock Bowers, Travis Kelce

Fantasy scoop: Rice's usage and production have increased each week of the season and he's found himself right back in the "lineup lock" mix. After underwhelming with a 2-19-1 receiving line on two targets in Week 1, Rice improved to 4-83-0 on six targets in Week 2 before leaping to 7-88-0 on nine targets last week. Rice handled a hefty 39% target share against Miami on Sunday and is enjoying career-high usage in terms of both snaps (79%) and route participation (75%) this season.

The fourth-year receiver is a strong fantasy WR2 against a Las Vegas defense that has yet to allow any WR touchdowns, though that's a bit fluky considering it has surrendered a total of five passing TDs (11th most).

Over/under: 48.5 (6th highest)

Win probability: Chiefs 68% (6th highest)

Denver Broncos @ San Francisco 49ers
Projected score: 49ers 26, Broncos 19

Lineup locks: Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, Jaylen Waddle, George Kittle

Fantasy scoop: Courtland Sutton's slow start has eliminated him from "lineup lock" consideration. The veteran wideout has been held to an 8-82-0 receiving line on 16 targets and has yet to reach 8.0 fantasy points in any game this season. His 18% target share is his lowest since his rookie season in 2018. On the plus side, his usage was up in Week 3 (23% target share) and he remains busy near the goal line (three end zone targets, third most among WRs). Consider him as no more than a flex.

Over/under: 44.1 (12th highest)

Win probability: 49ers 74% (4th highest)

Los Angeles Chargers @ Seattle Seahawks
Projected score: Seahawks 28, Chargers 16

Lineup lock: Jaxon Smith-Njigba

Fantasy scoop: Omarion Hampton has a pair of touchdowns and sits 10th among RBs in carries this season, but his usage -- combined with a tough Week 4 matchup -- makes him a risky fantasy play. The second-year back has been a nonfactor (almost literally) in the passing game, having totaled just 21 yards on three targets (with both of his catches coming in Week 2). As a result, he's been held below 8.5 fantasy points in two out of three games despite the good rushing production.

Hampton, who played on a season-low 42% of snaps in Week 3, will now face a Seattle defense that has allowed 2.9 yards per carry (second lowest) and the fifth-fewest fantasy points to RBs this season. Hampton is best viewed as a fringe RB2.

Over/under: 43.5 (13th highest)

Win probability: Seahawks 87% (3rd highest)

Detroit Lions @ Carolina Panthers
Projected score: Lions 29, Panthers 27

Lineup locks: Bryce Young, Jahmyr Gibbs, Chuba Hubbard, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Sam LaPorta

Fantasy scoop: Young fell back to earth last week, but that shouldn't stop you from streaming him here in Week 4. Despite the quiet fantasy day (13.6 points), the 2023 first overall pick still managed 291 passing yards and now leads the NFL in that category through three games.

Young threw three TD passes in both Weeks 1 and 2 and also paces the league in expected passing TDs. We could use more rushing production (3-16-1 this season), but we may not need it this week against a Detroit defense that has allowed the most passing yards and QB fantasy points, as well as the second-most passing TDs (nine). Josh Allen, Geno Smith and Tyler Shough each scored 23-plus points against Detroit this season.

Over/under: 56.0 (Highest)

Win probability: Lions 54% (15th highest)

Atlanta Falcons @ New Orleans Saints
Projected score: Saints 26, Falcons 22

Lineup locks: Tyler Shough, Bijan Robinson, Chris Olave, Drake London

Fantasy scoop: Travis Etienne Jr. is expected to miss time, which leaves New Orleans with a three-headed committee featuring Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson. Kamara figures to lead the group, but considering his lack of production last season (1 TD, 9.7 fantasy PPG) and limited usage this season (63 yards on 24 snaps over two games), the 31-year-old is a long shot to play a "feature back" role.

Instead, Miller (49 yards and one TD on 15 touches in his two games) and Donaldson (9 yards on five touches over three games) will be plenty involved, with Miller being a candidate to lead the group in carries. Kamara is a low-ceiling flex option against an Atlanta defense that has allowed 3.1 yards per carry and the fourth-fewest fantasy points to RBs.

Over/under: 47.7 (7th highest)

Win probability: Saints 62% (7th highest)

stories.headline: Second Hull player flips car outside training ground - reports
stories.summary: A second Hull player has been reported to have flipped his car in an accident close to the club's training ground in Cottingham.
stories.body:
A second Hull player has been reported to have flipped his car in an accident close to the club's training ground in Cottingham.

A photograph of a Mercedes car, which had rolled onto its side on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham, has been posted on social media.

In a similar incident three weeks ago, Hull midfielder Sorba Thomas escaped uninjured after rolling his car onto its roof on the same narrow residential street.

It has been reported that French summer signing Lucas Gourna-Douath was the driver in Thursday's accident.

Humberside Police said: "Officers and emergency services were called to reports of a single vehicle road traffic collision on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham at around 8.30am this morning (Thursday, 1 October 2026).

"Thankfully, no one was injured as a result of the collision."

The Press Association has contacted Hull for comment.

- New Hull signing Sorba Thomas unhurt after flipping car near Premier League side's training ground

Thomas' Land Rover was pictured upside down on Millhouse Woods Lane after an incident on Sept. 11.

In response, local councillor Phil Redshaw said on Facebook that he had contacted the club earlier that week, urging them to remind players to drive with more care when approaching the training ground.

He said: "I only wrote to the club on Sunday, asking them to remind staff to drive with more care and attention when heading for the training ground!"

stories.headline: Ohtani or Crow-Armstrong at No. 1? Your way-too-early top 50 players for 2027
stories.summary: The 2026 fantasy baseball season just ended, but Eric Karabell is already thinking about 2027.
stories.body:
Chicago Cubs OF Pete Crow-Armstrong was not only the best baseball player in 2026, but he easily led the field when it came to roto/category-based fantasy formats as well. Crow-Armstrong was a true five-category roto option, hitting .278 with 45 home runs, 107 RBIs and 41 stolen bases. He easily led the final Player Rater, followed by the likely Cy Young award winners in each league, while San Diego Padres OF/2B Fernando Tatis Jr. and Houston Astros DH/OF Yordan Alvarez rounded out the top five.

Can we make a case for PCA over Los Angeles Dodgers DH/SP Shohei Ohtani for 2027 roto drafts? I think we can. After all, we could make the case that New York Yankees OF Aaron Judge deserved the top nod over Ohtani entering 2026. Judge was a dominant offensive player in three of the prior four seasons, hitting .311 or above three times, providing massive power and stealing double-digit bases. Things didn't quite work out in 2026. Still, Ohtani's pitching prowess placed him ahead for ADP.

Ohtani, 32, made only 14 pitching starts in 2026, though they were awesome starts (1.79 ERA, 0.95 WHIP). At the plate, Ohtani delivered his worst season as a Dodger, hitting "only" .275 with 30 home runs and 11 stolen bases in 139 games. That isn't special. The combination of the pitching and hitting numbers, however, remains special. It differentiates Ohtani, especially in fantasy leagues that permit the use of all his statistics concurrently.

Perhaps PCA, Judge or Kansas City Royals SS Bobby Witt Jr. can overcome that, but as a two-way player option, Ohtani remains No. 1.

Way-too-early top 50 category-based rankings for 2027
1. Shohei Ohtani, DH/SP, Dodgers: It was not his best season, but he clearly intends to keep pitching, and the combination of massive power numbers with (hopefully) 100-plus innings pitched remains unmatched. Remember, as awesome as Crow-Armstrong was in 2026, Ohtani did hit .310 with 54 home runs and 59 stolen bases in 2024, when he did not pitch. He certainly can match Crow-Armstrong offensively.

2. Pete Crow-Armstrong, OF, Cubs: As amazing as Crow-Armstrong's season was, imagine if he plays at that top level for all six months of 2027. After all, he was hitting only .237 with seven home runs entering June.

3. Bobby Witt Jr., SS, Royals: Back tightness cost him a few weeks in July and his power suffered, yet he still finished seventh among hitters on the Player Rater. He is only 26 and perhaps a future MVP.

4. Aaron Judge, OF, Yankees: Just when you wanted to believe he was durable (he missed a mere 14 games over the previous two seasons), he played just two months in 2026. His offensive upside is such that he remains worth a top-5 pick in 2027.

5. Elly De La Cruz, SS, Cincinnati Reds: He may never steal 67 bases again, but it's worth it as he delivered his best batting average. After a standout 30/30 season in 2026, there is reasonable 40/40 upside lurking here.

6. Fernando Tatis Jr., OF/2B, Padres: Forget the first half of his 2026 season. A monster second half -- with top power -- pushed him into the No. 2 spot among hitters in the final Player Rater.

7. Juan Soto, OF, New York Mets: Injuries truncated his season, but the plate discipline and power remain. He can always steal bases again if he feels like doing so.

8. Yordan Alvarez, OF, Astros: He's back! Alvarez returned to elite, four-category production, posting career-best numbers.

9. Junior Caminero, 3B, Tampa Bay Rays: It is indeed rare for any player to deliver multiple seasons of 40 home runs before turning 25, but what if Caminero keeps improving?

10. Jacob Misiorowski, SP, Milwaukee Brewers: The pending NL Cy Young Award winner delivered one of the top pitching seasons of the century, striking out 252 hitters. Might he get hurt eventually? Sure. But look at the hitters ranked ahead of him. Anyone might get hurt.

11. Cam Schlittler, SP, Yankees: And here is the obvious AL Cy Young Award winner. We knew he was good, but this good?

12. Tarik Skubal, SP, Dodgers: We're not sure where he pitches in 2027, but assuming it isn't Denver (it won't be Denver), he should be great again.

13. Jackson Chourio, OF, Brewers: He has started his career with three consecutive 20/20 seasons, with the implication being he is merely getting started.

14. Jose Ramirez, 3B, Cleveland Guardians: He is on the other side of 30 and there are legit concerns after a powerless season. We say he isn't done yet.

15. James Wood, OF, Washington Nationals: An oblique injury cost him a month and sapped power, otherwise he might have hit 40 home runs.

16. Corbin Carroll, OF, Arizona Diamondbacks: It was not his best season, but it's hard to complain about four consecutive 20/20 campaigns to begin a career.

17. Julio Rodriguez, OF, Seattle Mariners: It was not his best season, either, but he still managed to produce his fifth consecutive 20/20 season to start his career.

18. Jordan Walker, OF, St. Louis Cardinals: Finally! A major breakout season put him in the conversation for fantasy MVP, as he finished ninth among hitters on the Rater. There is 40/30 upside here.

19. Jackson Merrill, OF, Padres: As with Tatis, he turned his season around and flirted with 30/30 numbers. He hasn't turned 24 yet.

20. Ronald Acuna Jr., OF, Atlanta Braves: He last reached 110 games played during the 2023 season, but he managed to reach 20/20 for the third time in 2026.

21. CJ Abrams, SS, Nationals: A solid performer prior to this season, the power made a huge jump -- and he surpassed 100 RBIs.

22. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, SP, Dodgers: All these Dodgers stars and this is the only guy joining Ohtani in the top 50. Another dominant season.

23. Cristopher Sanchez, SP, Philadelphia Phillies: A few rough outings elevated his ERA/WHIP, but the strikeouts and 18 wins were there.

24. Dylan Cease, SP, Toronto Blue Jays: Year 1 in Toronto featured his best ERA/WHIP since 2022, with his sixth consecutive season of 200-plus strikeouts.

25. Paul Skenes, SP, Pittsburgh Pirates: His ERA roughly doubled from his career mark to 3.82, but it wasn't really all that bad. Good news: No WBC in 2027!

26. Pete Alonso, 1B, Baltimore Orioles: He's the first player to win an RBI title in each league. We can always count on durability, power and perhaps safe batting average, too. He was the No. 11 on the Player Rater.

27. Matt Olson, 1B, Braves: He is a lot like Alonso, but he isn't quite Alonso, is he? Still, it is nice to count on 162 games and solid power every year.

28. Bryce Harper, 1B/OF, Phillies: He had a solid season. He played in all 162 games and added outfield eligibility, but is he elite? Harper finished 29th among hitters on the Rater, a few spots after Olson.

29. Kyle Schwarber, OF, Phillies: Elite power, but a batting average drain in roto formats.

30. Nick Kurtz, 1B, Athletics: Don't shy away from investing here for 2027. His power and plate discipline are real.

31. Miguel Vargas, 3B/1B, Chicago White Sox: What a fantastic breakout season -- even in roto, where he finished 14th among hitters on the Rater. He was a top-5 hitter in points formats.

32. Brice Turang, 2B, Brewers: This five-category provider hasn't fully tapped into his power and he may never steal 50 again, but this version of Turang works.

33. Oneil Cruz, OF, Pirates: No longer an automatic out versus left-handed pitchers, there remains power upside here.

34. Konnor Griffin, SS, Pirates: No, he did not contend for top rookie honors, but this is a future star. His power and plate discipline will develop quickly.

35. Francisco Lindor, SS, Mets: A calf injury cost him two months. Don't forget he reached 30/30 in two of the previous three seasons. It can happen again.

36. Chris Sale, SP, Braves: He turns 38 in March. 2026 was another great season, but with fewer innings -- and some mild reason for caution.

37. Garrett Crochet, SP, Boston Red Sox: He made only six starts, but let's remember what he achieved during the 2025 campaign. It was electric.

38. Max Fried, SP, Yankees: He delivered excellent numbers in a truncated campaign. Don't assume injuries complicate future seasons.

39. Kevin McGonigle, SS/3B, Detroit Tigers: This fantastic rookie was a points-league star, but the arrow points up for power, speed in roto, too.

40. Sal Stewart, 1B/3B, Reds: This fantastic rookie wasn't just a power option, as he stole 15 bases and hit for a decent batting average.

41. Rafael Devers, 1B, San Francisco Giants: He showed excellent power in his first full Giants season. There's no reason to believe it stops anytime soon.

42. Ben Rice, 1B, Yankees: His numbers look a lot like what Devers delivered. The power is real, but his days of playing catcher are over.

43. Jazz Chisholm Jr., 2B, Yankees: That was his worst MLB season for OPS, but he still has power and still steals bases.

44. Randy Arozarena, OF, Mariners: Here's an underrated, often-overlooked veteran who boasts six consecutive 20/20 seasons. He's not the reason the Mariners struggled.

45. Jesus Luzardo, SP, Phillies: Even a late-season IL stint could not prevent him from top-10 starter status. He has more than 200 K's in three out of four seasons.

46. Chase Burns, SP, Reds: Similarly, his late-season IL stint means little in the big picture. He boasted a top-10 strikeout rate as well, and he won 15 out of 18 decisions.

47. Gavin Williams, SP, Guardians: He went from a decent strikeout option to leading the AL -- and quickly. He is another ace to build around.

48. Jac Caglianone, OF/1B, Royals: The No. 43 hitter on the Rater boasts massive power upside and his .289 batting average was a nice surprise. Don't be surprised when he supplies at least 35 home runs in future seasons.

49. Chandler Simpson, OF, Rays: Investors will not enjoy home runs or RBIs with this pick, but Simpson hit .306 with 46 stolen bases, filling a need in roto formats. He ranked 18th among hitters on the final Player Rater.

50. Mason Miller, RP, Padres: Baseball's preeminent reliever (129 strikeouts!) goes even earlier than this in points formats. One can also make the case for Cleveland's Cade Smith, Toronto's Louis Varland and Philadelphia's Jhoan Duran in this range after their awesome seasons.

Other hitters under consideration: Drake Baldwin, C, Braves; Carson Benge, OF, Mets; Michael Harris II, OF, Braves; Alec Burleson, 1B/OF, Cardinals; Otto Lopez, SS, Miami Marlins; Yandy Diaz, 1B, Rays; Zach Neto, SS, Los Angeles Angels

Other pitchers under consideration: Drew Rasmussen, Rays; Zack Wheeler, Phillies; Logan Gilbert, Mariners; Nolan McLean, Mets

stories.headline: Wings' Ogunbowale scores record 45 to force Game 3 vs. Valkyries
stories.summary: Arike Ogunbowale delivered a record-breaking performance with the Wings' season on the line, scoring 45 points, including a tying 3-pointer to force overtime, to help Dallas force a deciding Game 3 against the Valkyries.
stories.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Arike Ogunbowale stood near Paige Bueckers and waited for the star guard to make a move on her dribble with the Dallas Wings trailing by three as the final seconds of regulation -- and their season -- ticked away.

Bueckers waved toward her backcourt mate, but she wasn't telling Ogunbowale to get out of the way. She was telling her to get open.

After all, Bueckers knew whom the hot hand was -- and it wasn't her.

Ogunbowale took a pass from Bueckers on the left baseline, dribbled toward the corner and hit an off-balance corner 3-pointer, sending the game to overtime and her on the way to a WNBA playoff-record 45 points as the Wings won a thriller 108-100 on Wednesday night, forcing a Game 3 in their first-round series.

The deciding game will be Friday night in San Francisco, where the Valkyries won the series opener by 24 points.

Golden State is trying to advance in the playoffs for the first time in the franchise's second season. The Wings are trying to reach the semifinals for the second time in six postseason appearances since moving to the Dallas area in 2016.

Ogunbowale opened the extra period of Game 2 by banking in a 3, then hit another one to put Dallas ahead for good at 103-100 with 1:46 remaining. A four-time All-Star, she easily topped her previous playoff best of 24 points after scoring 10 points on just seven shots in the series opener.

"We felt like we got pushed around out there when we played in San Francisco, and especially me, personally, I don't feel like I was aggressive," Ogunbowale said. "I didn't know what I would score. I was going to shoot regardless because I just feel like seven shots isn't enough to win playoffs and I have to be aggressive whether it's going in or not."

Bueckers, the 2025 No. 1 overall pick and Rookie of the Year who is in her first playoff series, was mired in a 3-for-13 shooting night that included an air ball on a 3-pointer with the Wings trailing by three in the final two minutes of regulation. But she assisted on Ogunbowale's tying 3, and again on a the banked 3 to start OT. Bueckers finished with 10 points and had four assists.

"For us to do what we did today without Paige having the type of game that she always has offensively for us, to come out with a win is huge," Wings coach Jose Fernandez said. "We had other people step up."

Ogunbowale's shot for a 93-93 tie with 4.1 seconds left in regulation of Game 2 was followed by Gabby Williams getting called for an offensive foul on the inbound play after a Golden State timeout.

That call was reversed on replay, so instead of Aziaha James having a chance to give Dallas the lead at the free throw line, there was a jump ball at center court with 3.0 seconds to go. After a scramble for the loose ball, Golden State's desperation shot was way off target and after the buzzer.

Williams scored 36 points, a career-high for regular season or playoffs, but she missed all six of her shots in the final 1:31 of overtime to finish 12-of-23 from the field.

"We got one at home, and we got to bring our best," Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said. "That was not our best. Tomorrow's got to be clear minds, clear focus, clear game plan, and then be ready to go for the game at home."

Ogunbowale scored 22 points in the fourth quarter and overtime -- 11 in each period. She passed her previous overall career high of 41 points with the 3 that put Dallas up for good.

Dallas' Alysha Clark tied her playoff career high with 21 points, and Aziaha James added 13.

Kaila Charles scored 14 points for the Valkyries, and Kayla Thornton had 13.

With the scored tied at 98 in the extra period, Ogunbowale and Tiffany Hayes had to be separated after making contact. Both were called for flagrant fouls, and each made a pair of free throws with 2:26 remaining.

The Valkyries didn't score again, shooting 2-of-12 in overtime.

stories.headline: Fantasy basketball: Players to know and position battles to watch during NBA preseason
stories.summary: Eric Moody points out which preseason NBA position battles could have big fantasy ramifications.
stories.body:
As the NBA gears up for an exciting training camp and preseason, fantasy basketball managers should keep a close eye on key position battles across the league.

Who wins and loses these competitions for starting spots and more minutes will go a long way toward shaping players' fantasy value. Unlike the NFL, where position battles often revolve around executing specific plays or packages, basketball's fight for playing time is far more nuanced. Success on the hardwood depends not just on individual skill but also on chemistry and fit with teammates.

After a busy offseason of roster changes and player movement, these looming position battles add an extra layer of intrigue as fantasy basketball draft season begins.

Portland Trail Blazers backcourt: Damian Lillard, Ja Morant, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Deni Avdija
Portland has a lot to sort out in the backcourt with Shaedon Sharpe (meniscus) sidelined for the next five months. Lillard and Morant should command major roles, but Holiday and Henderson also need minutes. Avdija adds another layer after averaging 24.2 points, 6.9 rebounds and 6.7 assists last season with much of the offense running through him.

What to watch for: How often Lillard and Morant's minutes are staggered, whether Avdija continues to initiate offense and if Henderson controls the second unit. If Henderson consistently gets 25-plus minutes with meaningful time on the ball, he moves into the late-round conversation.

New Orleans Pelicans center: Derik Queen, Yves Missi
Queen and Missi give New Orleans two very different options at center. Queen brings more scoring and playmaking, while Missi offers rebounding, rim protection and athleticism. Queen averaged 5.3 assists per 36 minutes as a rookie, which gives New Orleans a level of creation at center that Missi doesn't provide.

What to watch for: Which big man gets the majority of the center minutes, who spends more time with the starters and who closes games. If Queen handles the larger role, his all-around offensive game gives him the stronger fantasy ceiling. If the split stays close, Missi can still help managers looking for rebounds and blocks.

Houston Rockets backcourt: Reed Sheppard, Fred VanVleet, Marcus Smart
Houston has another crowded backcourt with VanVleet returning and the defensive-minded Smart joining the rotation. Sheppard should remain part of the mix after averaging 13.5 points in 26.2 minutes last season, but Amen Thompson also handles the ball and can initiate offense. Sheppard also averaged 1.5 steals per game, which gives him a useful fantasy floor even if his playmaking role stays limited.

What to watch for: Whether Sheppard runs the offense when VanVleet sits or spends most of his time off the ball. If Houston gives him regular creation work and closing minutes, he becomes much more appealing in standard leagues. If not, his value will depend more heavily on threes and steals.

Orlando Magic backcourt: Jalen Suggs, Anthony Black, Jase Richardson

Suggs enters camp with the inside track to start, but Black's development gives Orlando another legitimate option in the backcourt. Black averaged 15.0 points in nearly 30 minutes per game last season and can contribute as both a scorer and facilitator. Richardson adds another young guard competing for rotation time.

What to watch for: Whether Black runs the second unit even when Suggs starts and whether he remains part of Orlando's closing five. He doesn't need the starting job to matter in fantasy. A role close to 30 minutes with regular ball-handling duties would keep him firmly in the standard-league mix.

Boston Celtics center: Neemias Queta, Mitchell Robinson
Boston can approach the center position in several different ways. Queta provides efficiency and rebounding, while Robinson gives the Celtics a strong interior presence. Robinson averaged 16.1 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per 36 minutes last season, which is why even a modest workload could matter in fantasy.

What to watch for: Whether Robinson consistently gets 20-25 minutes with the main rotation and which center is trusted late in games. If Boston is comfortable giving Robinson that workload, his rebounds and blocks could make him useful even without starting. If Queta keeps the larger role, he remains the safer late-round option.

Charlotte Hornets center: Moussa Diabate, Hannes Steinbach

Diabate earned a significant role last season with his rebounding, defense and energy, but Steinbach gives Charlotte a different option at center. The rookie averaged 18.5 points and 11.8 rebounds at Washington in his one season of college and brings more size and offensive versatility. Naz Reid's ability to play center could also squeeze the available minutes.

What to watch for: Whether Charlotte trusts Steinbach enough defensively to keep him on the floor with the regular rotation. If he is consistently getting 20-25 minutes, he becomes a viable late-round target. If not, Diabate remains the safer source of rebounds and defensive stats.

Utah Jazz backcourt rotation: Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Isaiah Collier, Ace Bailey
George enters the season with the most secure role after putting up 23.6 PPG last season, but Utah still has plenty to sort out around him. Peterson gives the Jazz another high-upside creator after being selected No. 2 overall in June, while Collier is trying to earn a larger share of the backcourt minutes. Bailey adds another layer because his size and scoring allow Utah to play bigger on the perimeter. He averaged 13.8 points as a rookie and showed more versatility as the season progressed.

What to watch for: Whether Peterson starts alongside George, how often Bailey plays with the primary lineup and whether Utah leans into bigger perimeter groups instead of using multiple guards together. Collier's minutes could be the most vulnerable if Peterson earns a large on-ball role and Bailey becomes a regular part of closing lineups. If that happens, Peterson could move firmly into the standard-league conversation, while Bailey would have a clearer path to a bigger fantasy role.

Denver Nuggets forward: Cameron Johnson, DeMar DeRozan
Johnson and DeRozan give Denver two very different offensive options. Johnson stretches the floor and doesn't need the ball to make an impact, while DeRozan provides more shot creation and playmaking. Johnson shot 43.0% from long range last season, making his spacing especially valuable alongside Denver's other stars.

What to watch for: Which player is on the floor to close games and how much creation responsibility DeRozan gets. If Johnson's 3-point volume rises, he can provide more scoring without needing more touches. DeRozan's value will depend more on whether Denver gives him enough opportunities to create with the ball.

Milwaukee Bucks backcourt: Ryan Rollins, Brayden Burries, Kevin Porter Jr.
Milwaukee has plenty of guards competing for opportunities alongside veteran Tyler Herro. Rollins is coming off a productive season after shooting 40.6% from 3-point range, Porter is returning from knee surgery and the rookie first-rounder Burries is trying to turn a strong summer into an immediate rotation role. Burries averaged 23.5 points and 2.0 steals during Summer League, but Milwaukee's veteran depth could make early minutes difficult to find.

What to watch for: Whether Burries is consistently part of the regular rotation, handles the ball with the second unit and gets minutes alongside the starters. If he clears 20 minutes regularly during the preseason, he becomes a late-round option. If not, he's better left on the watch list to start the season.

stories.headline: After a shocking offseason, the Flyers fight regression
stories.summary: Philly was one of the NHL's biggest surprise teams last season -- and now has to back up the bold moves of its GM.
stories.body:
VOORHEES, N.J. -- The Philadelphia Flyers were one of the NHL's genuine surprises last season, making the playoffs for the first time since 2020 and advancing to the second round with a series win over the rival Pittsburgh Penguins.

General manager Danny Briere had overseen their rebuild since 2023. "Brick by brick," he said, sitting in his office at the team's practice facility. "Not trying to get ahead of ourselves. Trying to do it right."

But this offseason the Flyers put the meticulous bricklaying on hold and attempted to just buy someone else's furnished mansion. They signed Anaheim Ducks center Leo Carlsson, 21, to a five-year, $90 million offer sheet in a move that changed the financial landscape of player salaries and nearly shifted the competitive balance in the NHL with it.

The moment it was announced, Briere started hearing from his peers.

"The one that kept coming back the most was, 'You do what's right for your team.' We all have different things to deal with. There's nothing wrong with what you did. You played by the rules and it's there for anybody to use," he said.

New Jersey Devils GM Sunny Mehta always thought it was possible that a team would back up the truck for a restricted free agent the way the Flyers did.

"The only thing that you just aren't sure about is the taboo of the offer sheet. Will people actually do this?" he said. "You hear people talk about this every year. Doing it is a whole separate story. And someone actually did it."

Philadelphia center Trevor Zegras knew Carlsson from their days together in Anaheim and was excited by Briere's bold move -- even if the Flyers group chat was eerily quiet. "Maybe guys were just hoping that it would end up going through. Maybe they didn't want to jinx it," Zegras said.

Whether it was jinxed or not, the Ducks matched the offer sheet, depriving the Flyers of a potential franchise center. But Briere's move changed things. Carlsson's $18 million annual cap hit, the highest in the NHL this season, reset the bar for other's contracts. That included one the Ducks had to give their leading goal scorer Cutter Gauthier, who eventually signed for six years at a $13.5 million annual cap hit.

Gauthier was drafted by the Flyers at No. 5 in 2022 but was traded to Anaheim after telling Briere he didn't want to play for Philadelphia. One theory that emerged in the wake of the Carlsson offer sheet -- shared with ESPN by a player agent -- was that Flyers ownership greenlit the contract as the ultimate long-term vengeance with Anaheim after the Gauthier saga.

"They probably want to say, 'Hey, Philly's a good spot to be in. Don't [mess] with us,'" the agent said.

Briere denied that the Flyers had targeted the Ducks.

"My job's a lot more important than trying to get back at people. Look, we're all competitive. We're all trying to win. That scenario was what we felt was the right one for us," he said. "It wasn't my goal to put Anaheim in that position or [Ducks GM] Pat Verbeek in that position. We had a great relationship with them. We just felt we had a chance to improve our team, not give up any of our roster players. It just made sense for us at that moment. It was nothing more than that."

The offer sheet's ancillary benefit was as an endorsement of the Flyers' progress.

"It was cool. Any time your general manager tries to do something to better the team, it feels good. Love the direction that we're headed," Zegras said.

"I hope they're rejuvenated by it, even though it didn't work," Briere said. "We believe in our team. They took a big step last year and we wanted to show them that it didn't go unnoticed."

But the general manager also hopes his young team doesn't get tripped up during that leap forward.

THEIR FIRST STEP into this season was an embarrassing stumble for the Flyers. The Penguins walked out of Philadelphia having drubbed their hosts 7-0 on Wednesday night, the largest margin of defeat in a season opener in Flyers' history.

"I honestly don't have an answer. I don't think we won a battle tonight. They did everything better than us," Tocchet said. "There are alarming things out there. I don't know if guys are reading their press clippings, but it wasn't good."

The word regression is used a lot in the NHL, whether it's a player trying to sustain a high shooting percentage or a team trying to build on an expected playoff berth. There are all sorts of reasons the Flyers could drop from their 98-point total from last season -- injuries, bad puck luck, a downtick in their goaltending performance -- but the one Briere is watching closely is overconfidence.

"The part that keeps me up at night is having some of your players feel complacent, feel like they've made it," he said. "I'm worried that coming back, they'll think it's a little easier than they realize. If that happens, we could have a setback."

He has used winger Matvei Michkov as a cautionary tale. He scored 26 goals in 80 games as a rookie before having what the team felt was an underwhelming follow-up, which included a callout about his conditioning from new coach Rick Tocchet. Briere said he hoped young forwards such as Denver Barkey and Calder Trophy candidate Porter Martone didn't fall into the same trap.

"We talk to them. We address it with them and that's all part of our development team to getting them ready, using examples and trying to prepare them for what to expect this year," he said.

Michkov, for his part, showed up to camp in great shape and with "pep in his step," according to Briere. "I think we saw him mature as the season went on last year. Everybody has a different path. You all wish that guys were like Sidney Crosby and were a total pro at 16 years old, but the reality is those [players] are really rare," he said.

Another player on a different path last season was Zegras, the 25-year-old center they acquired from Anaheim in June 2025. Both Briere and Tocchet challenged him to level up his game with the Flyers, and Zegras reignited his star in the NHL: Scoring 26 goals and 41 assists in 81 games, and earning a four-year, $36.5 million contract extension.

Briere isn't concerned about Zegras falling into old habits now that he has signed an extension.

"We've had many talks about facing the pressure, playing in big games, not afraid of big moments. I was really, really impressed with how he handled it, how he played hard, because that was a little bit of a knock on him early in his career," Briere said. "I think he's matured a lot, took a big step forward last year. He started understanding better. He never played in a playoff game before, and that experience was huge for him."

To that end, the worst thing that happened to the Flyers last season might end up being the best thing for them: getting mauled by the Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes in a second-round sweep.

"They were good. They were experienced. They knew how to handle it and they did a better job," Briere said. "But that experience for us was I think amazing."

That also goes for the Flyers' journey to a playoff berth, winning huge games down the stretch, and their first-round win over the Penguins, in which Philadelphia jumped out to a 3-0 series lead before holding off Pittsburgh's rally to win in six games.

"Last year was such a different experience," Flyers winger Travis Konecny said. "Coming back, we're still talking about it. So that tells me guys have had it in the back of their head all summer. They're hungry. They want more."

Briere won't make any grand proclamations about the Flyers this season.

"You're not going to like my answer. I know it's boring. But we're still a young team," he said. "We expect it to be harder. For me, it's exciting, because we're at a time now where you want to see how your guys handle the hard. We're not going to creep up on anyone this year."

Briere hoped Carlsson might be part of that group for the Flyers, but he's wearing a different shade of orange and black this season. If the opportunity presents itself again, Briere said he won't hesitate to aggressively augment an already promising roster.

"We were a bad team for way too long to just throw away the cap space that we've built and the freedom that we're able to have. We're not going to be reckless about it," he said. "If something comes up that makes sense, we won't be afraid to take a swing again."

stories.headline: Max Verstappen steps in for GT race at Portimão amid two F1 triple-headers
stories.summary: This weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will be the second of seven consecutive race weekends for Max Verstappen after he confirmed he has added a GT race at Portimão to his schedule for later this month.
stories.body:
This weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will be the second of seven consecutive race weekends for Max Verstappen after he confirmed he has added a GT race at Portimão to his schedule for later this month.

Verstappen's GT team, Verstappen Racing, is participating in the GT World Challenge this year, but two of its drivers, Dani Juncadella and Jules Gounon, have a World Endurance Championship calendar clash with the Portuguese round on Oct. 18.

The race at Portimão does not clash with an F1 weekend -- falling between the Singapore Grand Prix and U.S. Grand Prix -- and Verstappen has confirmed he will step in to make sure his team has a full driver line-up.

"I know that two of my drivers won't be part of the line-up, so two other drivers need to step in and I'm looking forward to it," he said.

"It's going to be a busy seven weeks, but we'll do it and I enjoy it anyway. So, yeah. Let's see what we can do there."

F1 is in the midst of one of its most intense periods of races in its 76-year history, with this weekend's race in Malaysia the second of nine scheduled grands prix in 11 weeks.

The Bahrain Grand Prix was originally meant to go ahead in April, but was cancelled due to the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran in the region.

Rather than scrap the round altogether, Bahrain and F1 came to an agreement with Malaysia to host the race 4,000 miles away at the Sepang International Circuit this weekend.

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: Where were today's drivers when F1 last raced at Sepang?

- Fernando Alonso refuses to watch F1 from the sofa while he still has 'fire' inside to do better

When asked how he was coping with the upcoming flurry of races, Verstappen joked that his apathy towards F1's controversial power unit regulations this year had made it easier to get in the right headspace.

"I think I had four or five months of very intense preparation -- deep mental preparation of not giving an F," he said with a smile on his face. "So, yeah, I just rock up."

Verstappen also raced for his GT team at this year's Nürburgring 24 Hours, which he has since referenced as the highlight of his 2026 season to date.

His best results in F1 this year have been four second place finishes in Austria, Hungary, Spain and Azerbaijan, but he remains hopeful he can go one better and win a grand prix before the end of 2026.

"I'm trying everything I can," he said. "We are scoring, of course, quite a few podiums now, but I want to win. That's what I'm here for.

"And I'm getting close, but I want to at least win one race this year. So I hope we can do it, of course, at some point. But yeah, we have some solid results."

stories.headline: AFL overreactions: Brisbane can't win the 2027 flag without Chris Fagan and Lachie Neale
stories.summary: The season might be over, but there is still plenty to talk about -- particularly at the Lions. Chris Fagan is gone, Lachie Neale is off to Collingwood, and suddenly Brisbane's future looks very different.
stories.body:
The season might be over, but there is still plenty to talk about -- particularly at the Lions. Chris Fagan is gone, Lachie Neale is off to Collingwood, and suddenly Brisbane's future looks very different.

Let's get to this week's overreactions column, where we judge the biggest takeaway as legitimate or irrational.

Brisbane can't win the 2027 premiership without Chris Fagan and Lachie Neale
Beloved Lions coach Chris Fagan revealed to his playing group on Thursday morning that he would be departing the club and drawing the curtain on one of the greatest coaching decades in football history.

Fagan coached Brisbane for 10 seasons and on Saturday afternoon became just the sixth man to lead a team to a premiership three-peat.

The 65-year-old joins dual Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale as off-season Lions departures. Earlier in the week, Neale informed the club of his intent to sign with Collingwood as an unrestricted free agent.

Verdict: Overreaction

The losses of Fagan and Neale are obviously immense, and one could argue they were the two most critical pieces to Brisbane's dynastic run. But does anyone really believe this club is now set to nosedive? I didn't think so.

Let's start with Fagan. He leaves behind a Hall of Fame-worthy legacy and some mammoth shoes to fill. But there may not be a club more prepared to fill them than the Lions. Football boss Danny Daly, who has been involved in the AFL for 26 years, is someone that's been both waiting in the wings and long touted as a future senior coach. Should he get the nod, there are many at clubland who believe he can carry on what Fagan has built.

And then there's Neale. Like Fagan, he departs with an all-time resume, but a reminder, he's 33 years of age and probably now behind Will Ashcroft in the club's midfield pecking order. Neale's void isn't one that must be plugged, necessarily, rather it will provide opportunity for others to step up and take on greater responsibility.

Brisbane has already shown it knows how to evolve. This club didn't win three premierships by relying solely on Fagan and Neale. Luke Hodge, for example, helped steady the ship in the early years of Fagan's tenure before the Lions' flag run began. And since then the club has continued to build a deep, talented list.

The Lions might be the second-oldest team on paper, but that's selling short their future. Harris Andrews, Josh Dunkley, Tom Doedee, Jarrod Berry, and Hugh McCluggage are all still on the right side of 30, while Kai Lohmann, Darcy Wilmot, Jaspa Fletcher, Will Ashcroft, Logan Morris, Ty Gallop, Levi Ashcroft, and Daniel Annable are all aged under 24.

The Fagan era is over. The Neale era is over. But that doesn't necessarily mean the Lions' era is, too.

-- Jake Michaels

stories.headline: Philadelphia Union, USMNT's Cavan Sullivan becomes youngest MLS Player of the Month
stories.summary: Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.
stories.body:
Philadelphia Union and United States men's national team midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.

At 16, Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player to start a game for the United States since Freddy Adu in 2006 when he was picked in Mauricio Pochettino's XI for Saturday's 4-1 friendly win vs. Peru.

He was one of 11 players -- including seven other teenagers -- to make their first appearances for the U.S. in that game against Peru.

Sullivan, who turned 17 on Sept. 28, came on as a substitute on Tuesday in the USMNT's 4-2 friendly win over Chile.

Sullivan has seven goals and 12 assists in 26 games for the Union, who have surged up to sixth place in the Eastern Conference in recent weeks. He has played 1,675 league minutes in MLS.

His 19 goal contributions are tied with Alphonso Davies (2018) for the second-most by a teenager in an MLS season, trailing only Diego Fagundez (20 in 2013).

Since returning from the World Cup break, the Union have recorded 32 points during a 12-game unbeaten streak, which is tied for the most points by a club in a 12-game span in MLS history. Sullivan has started all 11 of those games, logging a goal contribution in eight of them.

Sullivan and the Union will return after the FIFA international break on Oc. 10 to host Real Salt Lake at Subaru Park (7:30 p.m. ET).

stories.headline: Lone'er Kavanagh: Win in 'dangerous' UFC 333 fight puts me in title contention
stories.summary: Brit Lone'er Kavanagh believes victory against Ramazonbek Temirov at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi could catapult him into flyweight title contention.
stories.body:
Brit Lone'er Kavanagh believes victory against Ramazonbek Temirov at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi could catapult him into flyweight title contention.

Kavanagh (10-2) is coming off a fight of the night defeat to Brandon Royval in July, a result that followed his breakout win over former champion Brandon Moreno in Mexico City earlier this year.

Uzbekistan's Temirov (20-3) is yet to taste defeat in the UFC octagon and is on a 12-fight win streak.

Kavanagh has said that a positive result in the Middle East could reignite his momentum in the featherweight division after the submission defeat to Royval last time out.

"I believe so. I'd like to think [it puts me into the featherweight title mix]," Kavanagh told ESPN.

"I think a win there puts me right back up there. He's a dangerous opponent. He's got some good wins under him, a lot of wins, but I think a win against him puts me right back up at the top. [I'm] always looking for a finish.

"He's dangerous. He throws big shots, he throws wild shots. He's constantly [moving] forwards. He likes to stand and bang. Those are the main things I think that stick out. Obviously he's got a good wrestling background as well.

"His main weapons are his heavy hands, and that excites me. I love fights like that and I think it's a good fight for me.

"Hopefully [another fight of the night], I'm looking for more performances of the night. Kavanagh was unranked before his decision win against Moreno and will now be a part of his second numbered UFC card, with his last fight at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on the night of Conor McGregor's ill-fated return against Max Holloway.

"It feels surreal, I'm very grateful I get these opportunities, being on a card with such big names, being high up, it's amazing. I'm very blessed," he said.

"If you told me 10 years ago I'd be fighting on cards like these, I'd have told you to do one, so it's very cool.

"It was an awesome opportunity to fight on that card, McGregor coming back, in Vegas, such a high-level fight. I'd like to think my style is entertaining as it is, I'm always looking to be in an entertaining fight and apart from that I just love fighting so just being in there is cool.

"I've gone from watching [UFC YouTube show] Embedded to actually being in it so that was cool!"

stories.headline: Roosters star admits he is torn on World Cup decision
stories.summary: Robert Toia has revealed he is still undecided if he wants to play for Australia or Tonga in the World Cup, less than a week out from teams being named.
stories.body:
Robert Toia has admitted he still doesn't know who he wants to play for at the World Cup, as the in-demand centre weighs up representing Tonga or Australia.

Toia is the highest-profile player caught in a tug-of-war between nations, with the World Cup just a fortnight ago and final squads to be announced next week.

Tonga coach Kristian Woolf had told AAP this week that Toia had indicated he wanted to represent the Pacific nation, after debuting for them last year.

Australia counterpart Kevin Walters has also made clear he believes the Sydney Roosters star is available for the Kangaroos, and he has not been told otherwise.

Toia has accepted he must make a decision soon, but remains uncertain what way he will go with Sunday's NRL grand final against Newcastle before this month's tournament.

"To be honest, I have not made my mind up," Toia told AAP.

"I just find it hard that I don't have a decision. I want to play for Tonga, it means so much to my family, myself and my people.

"I went over to Tonga last year and you can see how much it means to them.

"But to have Australia on your resume. Just to play for Australia, in my second year, I find it such a massive achievement. That's what I'm kind of weighing up."

Beyond Toia, Woolf also believes Sydney Roosters teammates Salesi Foketi and Siua Wong want to play for Tonga in the global showpiece.

Queensland winger Jojo Fifita revealed this week he too was still undecided, weighing up whether to play for Australia, New Zealand or Tonga.

Fifita told AAP he'd had discussions with all three nations, although he was not named in the Kiwis' initial 40-man squad.

Walters has said both Jojo and his brother David are under consideration for Australia's World Cup squad.

In better news for Tonga, Dolphins halfback Isaiya Katoa has confirmed he will be fit for the tournament after a syndesmosis injury in the preliminary-final loss to the Roosters.

"I don't need surgery. I will be able to play in the World Cup," Katoa said.

"I immediately knew I had done something, so I was definitely happy once I got the scans back it wasn't too bad and I will be able to represent Tonga."

Complicating matters for players who are weighing up their future is the fact Australian representatives stand to earn $40,000 by playing in the tournament.

AAP is aware of coaches and players who are concerned that may prompt some players to choose the Kangaroos in order to benefit their families.

But Katoa said it would never be a factor for him.

"I'd never look at the price tag, it's always where my heart is at," he said.

"I've always said my heart is at Tonga and if it wasn't for Tonga I am half-Cook Islands as well. So if it wasn't for Tonga, I would go Cook Islands."

Meanwhile it is understood Tonga will pick former St George Illawarra half Talatau Amone in their squad for the tournament.

Amone has not played since he was deregistered by the NRL in 2023 for assault. Tonga are still yet to learn if he will be cleared to play in the tournament.

He can return to the NRL next year, and starred on his return to Queensland Cup with Wynnum-Manly in recent months.
